model_doc: The CSM platform's semantic model (CLAUDE.md §3 Semantic layer). Read-only. Reads the app's Postgres tables plus the `semantic` views, which are the SQL twins of values the app derives in Python (dependency state, progress units, stage states, deal amounts). Tests pin those views to the Python logic, so numbers here always match the app.

sources.name: users
sources.doc: Internal staff and client users. Access roles live elsewhere; this is who someone is.

fields.name: is_internal
fields.doc: True for Shearwater staff, false for client users ('client_external').

sources.name: clients
sources.doc: A stable organisation: a client or a prospect (a prospect has opportunities but no engagement yet).

sources.name: engagement_types
sources.doc: An engagement type (QuickStart, Migration): its stage vocabulary and deliverable kinds live in the app.

sources.name: work_units
sources.doc: A unit of leaf-level work, which is what progress is measured in: each listed leaf deliverable counts once, and children tracked by count on a bulk-count parent count once each (a 99-tile dashboard is 99 units). Matches the app's progress bars exactly.

fields.name: is_done
fields.doc: 'listed' (a real deliverable row) or 'counted' (a child tracked only by count).

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Share of work units that are done, 0–1.

views.name: portfolio
views.doc: Every open engagement with its progress and how long it's been running.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     clients_0."name" as "client_name",
     base."name" as "engagement_name",
     engagement_types_0."display_name" as "type_name",
     base."status" as "status",
     FLOOR((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM LOCALTIMESTAMP)-EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM base."started_at"))/86400.0) as "running_days",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN work_units_0."pipeline_status"='done' THEN work_units_0."units" END),0) as "done_units",
     COALESCE(SUM(work_units_0."units"),0) as "total_units",
     (COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN work_units_0."pipeline_status"='done' THEN work_units_0."units" END),0))*1.0/(NULLIF(COALESCE(SUM(work_units_0."units"),0),0)) as "progress"
  FROM public.engagements as base
   LEFT JOIN public.clients AS clients_0
    ON clients_0."id"=base."client_id"
   LEFT JOIN public.engagement_types AS engagement_types_0
    ON engagement_types_0."key"=base."type_key"
   LEFT JOIN semantic.work_units AS work_units_0
    ON work_units_0."engagement_id"=base."id"
  WHERE ((base."status"='active') or (base."status"='paused'))
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
  ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST,2 ASC NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: by_type
views.doc: Open engagements per type and status.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     engagement_types_0."display_name" as "type_name",
     base."status" as "status",
     COUNT(1) as "engagement_count"
  FROM public.engagements as base
   LEFT JOIN public.engagement_types AS engagement_types_0
    ON engagement_types_0."key"=base."type_key"
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: active_stage_mix
views.doc: Which stages are active right now, across every open engagement.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     engagement_types_0."display_name" as "type_name",
     engagement_stages_0."stage_label" as "stage_label",
     COUNT(DISTINCT base."id") as "engagement_count"
  FROM public.engagements as base
   LEFT JOIN semantic.engagement_stages AS engagement_stages_0
    ON engagement_stages_0."engagement_id"=base."id"
   LEFT JOIN public.engagement_types AS engagement_types_0
    ON engagement_types_0."key"=base."type_key"
  WHERE ((base."status"='active') or (base."status"='paused')) and (engagement_stages_0."state"='active')
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: needs_attention_list
views.doc: Everything that needs someone's attention: flagged blocks, stale block flags, and started work held up by a dependency.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     clients_0."name" as "client_name",
     engagements_0."name" as "engagement_name",
     base."kind_label" as "kind_label",
     base."name" as "name",
     base."pipeline_status" as "pipeline_status",
     base."dep_state" as "dep_state",
     base."blocked_reason" as "blocked_reason"
  FROM semantic.deliverable_facts as base
   LEFT JOIN public.engagements AS engagements_0
    ON engagements_0."id"=base."engagement_id"
   LEFT JOIN public.clients AS clients_0
    ON clients_0."id"=base."client_id"
  WHERE base."needs_attention" and ((engagements_0."status"='active') or (engagements_0."status"='paused'))
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
  ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: overdue_by_assignee
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     assignee_0."user_name" as "user_name",
     COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_overdue" THEN 1 END) as "overdue_count",
     COALESCE(SUM(base."hours_estimated"),0) as "estimated_hours"
  FROM semantic.deliverable_facts as base
   LEFT JOIN public.engagements AS engagements_0
    ON engagements_0."id"=base."engagement_id"
   LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT id, display_name AS user_name, user_type::text AS user_type, is_admin, is_contractor, status, created_at
    FROM public.users
  ) AS assignee_0
    ON assignee_0."id"=base."internal_assignee_user_id"
  WHERE base."is_overdue" and ((engagements_0."status"='active') or (engagements_0."status"='paused'))
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: status_mix
views.doc: How many deliverables sit in each pipeline status, per kind.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     base."kind_label" as "kind_label",
     base."pipeline_status" as "pipeline_status",
     COUNT(1) as "deliverable_count"
  FROM semantic.deliverable_facts as base
  WHERE COALESCE(NOT base."not_applicable",TRUE)
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: team_load
views.doc: Internal people's open assignments, by role.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     users_0."user_name" as "user_name",
     COUNT(CASE WHEN base."role"='owner' THEN 1 END) as "owned",
     COUNT(1) as "assignments"
  FROM (
    SELECT engagement_id, user_id, role::text AS role, viewer_scope FROM public.engagement_memberships
  ) as base
   LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT id, display_name AS user_name, user_type::text AS user_type, is_admin, is_contractor, status, created_at
    FROM public.users
  ) AS users_0
    ON users_0."id"=base."user_id"
   LEFT JOIN public.engagements AS engagements_0
    ON engagements_0."id"=base."engagement_id"
  WHERE (users_0."user_type"='internal') and ((engagements_0."status"='active') or (engagements_0."status"='paused'))
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: pipeline_by_stage
views.doc: Open pipeline per stage, in pipeline order.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     base."stage_label" as "stage_label",
     base."stage_order" as "stage_order",
     COUNT(1) as "deal_count",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) THEN base."amount" END),0) as "open_pipeline",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) THEN base."weighted_amount" END),0) as "weighted_pipeline"
  FROM semantic.opportunity_facts as base
  WHERE COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE)
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY 2 ASC NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: forecast_by_quarter
views.doc: Per close quarter: won, commit, best case and open pipeline, raw and weighted.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     DATE_TRUNC('quarter', base."close_date") as "close_quarter",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN base."amount" END),0) as "won_amount",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) and (base."effective_forecast_category"='commit') THEN base."amount" END),0) as "commit_amount",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) and (base."effective_forecast_category"='best_case') THEN base."amount" END),0) as "best_case_amount",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) THEN base."amount" END),0) as "open_pipeline",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) THEN base."weighted_amount" END),0) as "weighted_pipeline"
  FROM semantic.opportunity_facts as base
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 1 ASC NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: win_rate_by_owner
views.doc: Win rate and totals per owner.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     owner_0."user_name" as "user_name",
     COUNT(1) as "deal_count",
     COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN 1 END) as "won_deals",
     COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_closed" THEN 1 END) as "closed_deals",
     (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN 1 END))*1.0/(NULLIF((COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_closed" THEN 1 END)),0)) as "win_rate",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN base."amount" END),0) as "won_amount",
     COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) THEN base."amount" END),0) as "open_pipeline"
  FROM semantic.opportunity_facts as base
   LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT id, display_name AS user_name, user_type::text AS user_type, is_admin, is_contractor, status, created_at
    FROM public.users
  ) AS owner_0
    ON owner_0."id"=base."owner_user_id"
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 6 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: by_source
views.doc: Where deals come from, and how they convert.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     base."source" as "deal_source",
     COUNT(1) as "deal_count",
     COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN 1 END) as "won_deals",
     (COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN 1 END))*1.0/(NULLIF((COUNT(CASE WHEN base."is_closed" THEN 1 END)),0)) as "win_rate",
     COALESCE(SUM(base."amount"),0) as "total_amount"
  FROM semantic.opportunity_facts as base
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 5 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: revenue_by_product
views.doc: Revenue by product, split into won and still open.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     products_0."name" as "product_name",
     products_0."pricing_model" as "pricing_model",
     (COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN base."is_won" THEN (items_0."quantity"*items_0."unit_price") END),0)) as "won_product_amount",
     (COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(NOT base."is_closed",TRUE) THEN (items_0."quantity"*items_0."unit_price") END),0)) as "open_product_amount"
  FROM semantic.opportunity_facts as base
   LEFT JOIN public.opportunity_line_items AS items_0
    ON items_0."opportunity_id"=base."opportunity_id"
   LEFT JOIN public.products AS products_0
    ON products_0."id"=items_0."product_id"
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: won_without_engagement_list
views.doc: Won deals that no engagement delivers yet: handoffs that haven't happened.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     clients_0."name" as "client_name",
     base."name" as "name",
     base."close_date" as "close_date",
     owner_0."user_name" as "user_name",
     COALESCE(SUM(base."amount"),0) as "total_amount"
  FROM semantic.opportunity_facts as base
   LEFT JOIN public.clients AS clients_0
    ON clients_0."id"=base."client_id"
   LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT id, display_name AS user_name, user_type::text AS user_type, is_admin, is_contractor, status, created_at
    FROM public.users
  ) AS owner_0
    ON owner_0."id"=base."owner_user_id"
  WHERE base."won_without_engagement"
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
  ORDER BY 3 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: weekly_activity
views.doc: Writes per week, by what was written.
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     (DATE_TRUNC('week', (base."occurred_at" + INTERVAL '1' DAY)) - INTERVAL '1' DAY) as "event_week",
     base."entity_type" as "entity_type",
     COUNT(1) as "event_count"
  FROM public.events as base
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY 1 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: completions_per_week
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     (DATE_TRUNC('week', (base."occurred_at" + INTERVAL '1' DAY)) - INTERVAL '1' DAY) as "event_week",
     COUNT(1) as "event_count"
  FROM public.events as base
  WHERE base."event_type"='deliverable_completed'
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 1 desc NULLS LAST
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

views.name: most_active
views.sql:
WITH __stage0 AS (
  SELECT 
     actor_0."user_name" as "user_name",
     COUNT(1) as "event_count"
  FROM public.events as base
   LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT id, display_name AS user_name, user_type::text AS user_type, is_admin, is_contractor, status, created_at
    FROM public.users
  ) AS actor_0
    ON actor_0."id"=base."actor_user_id"
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 2 desc NULLS LAST
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT row_to_json(finalStage) as row FROM __stage0 AS finalStage

malloy_text:
##" The CSM platform's semantic model (CLAUDE.md §3 Semantic layer). Read-only. Reads the app's
##" Postgres tables plus the `semantic` views, which are the SQL twins of values the app derives in
##" Python (dependency state, progress units, stage states, deal amounts). Tests pin those views to
##" the Python logic, so numbers here always match the app.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- people and clients

#" Internal staff and client users. Access roles live elsewhere; this is who someone is.
# Postgres enums are cast to text here; Malloy doesn't read user-defined types directly.
source: users is postgres.sql("""
  SELECT id, display_name AS user_name, user_type::text AS user_type, is_admin, is_contractor, status, created_at
  FROM public.users
""") extend {
  primary_key: id
  #" True for Shearwater staff, false for client users ('client_external').
  dimension: is_internal is user_type = 'internal'
  measure: user_count is count()
}

#" A stable organisation: a client or a prospect (a prospect has opportunities but no engagement yet).
source: clients is postgres.table('public.clients') extend {
  primary_key: id
  rename: client_name is name
  measure: client_count is count()
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- engagements

#" An engagement type (QuickStart, Migration): its stage vocabulary and deliverable kinds live in the app.
source: engagement_types is postgres.table('public.engagement_types') extend {
  primary_key: key
  rename: type_name is display_name
}

#" A unit of leaf-level work, which is what progress is measured in: each listed leaf deliverable
#" counts once, and children tracked by count on a bulk-count parent count once each
#" (a 99-tile dashboard is 99 units). Matches the app's progress bars exactly.
source: work_units is postgres.table('semantic.work_units') extend {
  #" 'listed' (a real deliverable row) or 'counted' (a child tracked only by count).
  dimension: is_done is pipeline_status = 'done'
  measure:
    total_units is units.sum()
    done_units is units.sum() { where: pipeline_status = 'done' }
    #" Share of work units that are done, 0–1.
    progress is done_units / nullif(units.sum(), 0)
}

#" Per engagement and stage, the derived stage state: done, active, upcoming or empty. Several
#" stages can be active at once on types whose stages follow their phases.
source: engagement_stages is postgres.table('semantic.engagement_stages') extend {
  measure:
    stage_rows is count()
    #" Stages currently active; can be more than one per engagement.
    active_stages is count() { where: state = 'active' }
}

#" A typed, time-bound unit of work for a client.
source: engagements is postgres.table('public.engagements') extend {
  primary_key: id
  rename: engagement_name is name
  except: slack_channel_id, internal_slack_channel_id, harvest_project_id, expected_scope, health, details
  join_one: clients with client_id
  join_one: engagement_types with type_key
  join_many: work_units on work_units.engagement_id = id
  join_many: engagement_stages on engagement_stages.engagement_id = id
  dimension:
    is_open is status = 'active' or status = 'paused'
    #" Days since the engagement started.
    running_days is days(started_at to now)
  measure:
    engagement_count is count()
    #" Active or paused.
    open_engagements is count() { where: is_open }

  #" Every open engagement with its progress and how long it's been running.
  view: portfolio is {
    where: is_open
    group_by: clients.client_name, engagement_name, engagement_types.type_name, status, running_days
    aggregate: work_units.done_units, work_units.total_units, work_units.progress
    order_by: client_name, engagement_name
  }

  #" Open engagements per type and status.
  view: by_type is {
    group_by: engagement_types.type_name, status
    aggregate: engagement_count
  }

  #" Which stages are active right now, across every open engagement.
  view: active_stage_mix is {
    where: is_open and engagement_stages.state = 'active'
    group_by: engagement_types.type_name, engagement_stages.stage_label
    aggregate: engagement_count
    order_by: engagement_count desc
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- deliverables

#" A tracked unit of work on an engagement (phase, milestone, dashboard, tile, curriculum module),
#" with its derived dependency state. Internal notes and client threads aren't modelled here.
source: deliverables is postgres.table('semantic.deliverable_facts') extend {
  primary_key: deliverable_id
  join_one: engagements with engagement_id
  join_one: clients with client_id
  join_one: assignee is users with internal_assignee_user_id
  #" blocked · maybe_unblocked · waiting · clear, from the manual flag plus blocker edges.
  dimension: dependency is dep_state
  measure:
    deliverable_count is count()
    done_count is count() { where: pipeline_status = 'done' }
    #" Flagged blocked, with something still unfinished (or nothing) to wait on.
    blocked_count is count() { where: dep_state = 'blocked' }
    #" Needs someone to act: a block flag, a stale block flag, or started work held up by a dependency. Not ordinary sequencing.
    attention_count is count() { where: needs_attention }
    #" Past its target date and not finished.
    overdue_count is count() { where: is_overdue }
    #" Sum of estimated hours.
    estimated_hours is hours_estimated.sum()

  #" Everything that needs someone's attention: flagged blocks, stale block flags, and started work held up by a dependency.
  view: needs_attention_list is {
    where: needs_attention and engagements.is_open
    group_by: clients.client_name, engagements.engagement_name, kind_label, name, pipeline_status, dep_state, blocked_reason
    order_by: client_name
  }

  #" Open, overdue deliverables by assignee.
  view: overdue_by_assignee is {
    where: is_overdue and engagements.is_open
    group_by: assignee.user_name
    aggregate: overdue_count, estimated_hours
    order_by: overdue_count desc
  }

  #" How many deliverables sit in each pipeline status, per kind.
  view: status_mix is {
    where: not not_applicable
    group_by: kind_label, pipeline_status
    aggregate: deliverable_count
    order_by: kind_label
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- team

#" Who is on which engagement, and in what role (owner, collaborator, viewer).
source: memberships is postgres.sql("""
  SELECT engagement_id, user_id, role::text AS role, viewer_scope FROM public.engagement_memberships
""") extend {
  join_one: users with user_id
  join_one: engagements with engagement_id
  measure:
    #" Engagement memberships, any role.
    assignments is count()
    #" Engagements the person owns (the single owner membership).
    owned is count() { where: role = 'owner' }

  #" Internal people's open assignments, by role.
  view: team_load is {
    where: users.is_internal and engagements.is_open
    group_by: users.user_name
    aggregate: owned, assignments
    order_by: assignments desc
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- opportunities

#" What opportunities are made of: fixed bid, time & materials, or retainer.
source: products is postgres.table('public.products') extend {
  primary_key: id
  rename: product_name is name
}

#" One product on an opportunity: quantity × its own unit price.
source: line_items is postgres.table('public.opportunity_line_items') extend {
  primary_key: id
  join_one: products with product_id
  #" Quantity × unit price.
  dimension: line_total is quantity * unit_price
  #" Sum of line totals.
  measure: line_amount is line_total.sum()
}

#" A deal on a client, with its amount (always the sum of its line items), effective probability and
#" forecast category (the stage's defaults unless overridden while open), and weighted amount.
source: opportunities is postgres.table('semantic.opportunity_facts') extend {
  primary_key: opportunity_id
  join_one: clients with client_id
  join_one: owner is users with owner_user_id
  join_many: items is line_items on items.opportunity_id = opportunity_id
  rename: deal_source is `source`
  dimension:
    #" The quarter the deal closes (or closed) in, for forecasting.
    close_quarter is close_date.quarter
    close_month is close_date.month
  measure:
    deal_count is count()
    #" Sum of deal amounts, open and closed.
    total_amount is amount.sum()
    #" Amount still in play: every open deal, at face value.
    open_pipeline is amount.sum() { where: not is_closed }
    #" Open deals weighted by their effective probability.
    weighted_pipeline is weighted_amount.sum() { where: not is_closed }
    #" Amount on Closed Won deals.
    won_amount is amount.sum() { where: is_won }
    #" Amount on Closed Lost deals.
    lost_amount is amount.sum() { where: is_lost }
    won_deals is count() { where: is_won }
    closed_deals is count() { where: is_closed }
    #" Won ÷ closed, by count of deals, 0–1.
    win_rate is won_deals / nullif(closed_deals, 0)
    #" Mean deal amount.
    average_deal is amount.avg()

  #" Open pipeline per stage, in pipeline order.
  view: pipeline_by_stage is {
    where: not is_closed
    group_by: stage_label, stage_order
    aggregate: deal_count, open_pipeline, weighted_pipeline
    order_by: stage_order
  }

  #" Per close quarter: won, commit, best case and open pipeline, raw and weighted.
  view: forecast_by_quarter is {
    group_by: close_quarter
    aggregate:
      won_amount
      commit_amount is amount.sum() { where: not is_closed and effective_forecast_category = 'commit' }
      best_case_amount is amount.sum() { where: not is_closed and effective_forecast_category = 'best_case' }
      open_pipeline
      weighted_pipeline
    order_by: close_quarter
  }

  #" Win rate and totals per owner.
  view: win_rate_by_owner is {
    group_by: owner.user_name
    aggregate: deal_count, won_deals, closed_deals, win_rate, won_amount, open_pipeline
    order_by: won_amount desc
  }

  #" Where deals come from, and how they convert.
  view: by_source is {
    group_by: deal_source
    aggregate: deal_count, won_deals, win_rate, total_amount
    order_by: total_amount desc
  }

  #" Revenue by product, split into won and still open.
  view: revenue_by_product is {
    group_by: items.products.product_name, items.products.pricing_model
    aggregate:
      won_product_amount is items.line_amount { where: is_won }
      open_product_amount is items.line_amount { where: not is_closed }
    order_by: won_product_amount desc
  }

  #" Won deals that no engagement delivers yet: handoffs that haven't happened.
  view: won_without_engagement_list is {
    where: won_without_engagement
    group_by: clients.client_name, name, close_date, owner.user_name
    aggregate: total_amount
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the event spine

#" Every write the app has made, append-only. Useful for activity and throughput over time.
source: events is postgres.table('public.events') extend {
  primary_key: id
  join_one: actor is users with actor_user_id
  dimension: event_week is occurred_at.week
  measure: event_count is count()

  #" Writes per week, by what was written.
  view: weekly_activity is {
    group_by: event_week, entity_type
    aggregate: event_count
    order_by: event_week desc
  }

  #" Deliverables completed per week.
  view: completions_per_week is {
    where: event_type = 'deliverable_completed'
    group_by: event_week
    aggregate: event_count
    order_by: event_week desc
  }

  #" Who's writing the most.
  view: most_active is {
    group_by: actor.user_name
    aggregate: event_count
    order_by: event_count desc
    limit: 10
  }
}
